summary:
Technical review of phase:g-release, iteration 1 (sub-mv4eqme2-01a6e8e9; commit f4f5f9b, tree 7c898c91; 42 artifacts). Every check I cite ran on that tree. The security draft phase-g-security-1.md (FINAL, verdict APPROVE, SEC-G-1 and SEC-G-2 minor, SEC-G-I1..I4 info) is folded in.

**Plan commands, verbatim.**
- g1: 242/242 (ev:ev-mv4ezs6l-01ac606f).
- g2: 27/27 (ev:ev-mv4ezsp4-01e98a8c).
- g3, as one argument with the suite lock held around the whole eccode run, green on the first run (ev:ev-mv4ezijm-016e7594). This is the only reviewer run of the full g3 command; security skipped the registry step by its loopback rule.
  - npm test: 2393 tests, 2385 pass, 0 fail, 8 skipped; NFR5 p95 56.8 ms;
  - browser: 28/28;
  - clean checkout: 448 files, npm install, npm test 2393 tests, 2383 pass, 0 fail, 10 skipped, npm start, health 200.

**Evidence table** (28 verified, 2 fake-only, 15 LIVE-DEPENDENT), checked against the spec's Testing table.
- No `verified` row rests on LIVE-P1, LIVE-P2, OQ-D5 or LIVE-M1 for its criterion as the spec scopes it.
- Weaker than written:
  - the spec's (I) parts of RS-29, RS-35, NFR3, NFR4 and RS-36 are not tagged or cited (TR-G-1). I performed all five read-only; all pass;
  - three Unverified cells point at the wrong blocker or list (TR-G-2);
  - ambiguous title fragments let the cited-run check pass on another file's test, as probe MT2 shows (TR-G-3);
  - RS-29's scan scope is narrower than its row (SEC-G-1).

**FU-62.** The final derive.js conforms to the derivation table row by row.

**Test strength.** All 5 of my g1 mutants are killed; the evidence-table check kills a row that cites the wrong run (MT1).

**T20.** The deviation is accepted on SEC-G-2's condition, which also covers my MS1.

**Clock shift.** shift-clock.mjs states its blind spots, and none is used in the code.

**README demo.** It runs verbatim on 127.0.0.1:3000 with a scratch database, but the sample text needs an undocumented diameter step (TR-G-5).

Decision: approve. No blocking or major finding; the minor findings TR-G-1, TR-G-2, TR-G-3, TR-G-5, SEC-G-1 and SEC-G-2 are routed before delivery with resolution conditions.

findings.title: The spec's (I) inspection parts are not tagged or cited for RS-29, RS-35, NFR3 and NFR4, and RS-36 says its inspection is not part of the evidence; this review performed all five
findings.detail:
**What the spec requires.** The Testing table gives an (I) part to:
- RS-29 (screenshots and submission);
- RS-35;
- RS-36 (F-TR-9);
- NFR3 (live report labelling);
- NFR4;
- NFR1 and NFR6.

**What the table shows.**
- It tags I only on RS-36 and NFR1.
- It marks RS-29, RS-35, NFR3 and NFR4 `verified` with D or B only.
- RS-36 is `verified` while its cell says the inspection 'is NOT part of this evidence'.
- No later review records these inspections: only the design and phase B reviews mention any.

**The inspections, done read-only in this review. All pass.**
- **RS-36 / FU-62:** derive.js against the brief's table and revision 2. Row by row it conforms, and no table stores a rescue status.
- **RS-29:** screenshots labelling-sandbox-stub-1280, six-questions-1280 and a11y-stranded-1280, plus docs/submission and the README: no secret value.
- **RS-35:** six-questions-1280 answers all six questions from codes.
- **NFR3:** both runners label their reports.
- **NFR4:** secrets come only from process.env, and .env.example secret entries are commented placeholders.

The statuses hold in substance. The table lacks only the I tags and the citation.

findings.title: Three Unverified cells point at the wrong blocker or list, and NFR2's suite tags omit D
findings.detail:
**RS-25.** It names 'LIVE-P1 (OQ-D5)', but no live file covers a lost capture answer, as the table's own 'Not covered by any live file' list says.

**RS-13 and RS-15.** They say that a void on the real Sandbox is 'part of the FU-52 list below'. That list has no plain void, and plain voids ARE covered by LIVE-P2 (journey-sandbox RS-32(b) asserts both authorizations VOIDED at PayPal).

**NFR2.** It is tagged B only but cites a D unit test.

No status changes.

findings.title: Ambiguous title fragments (RS-03, RS-22, RS-27) let the cited-run check pass on another file's test
findings.detail:
**The ambiguity.** The cited fragments occur in more than one test file:
- 'RS-03: fake_model:': extract-degraded and unit/ai/fake;
- 'RS-22: the second capture is declined': capture-compensation and execute;
- 'RS-27: another customer': four API files.

A TAP log carries no file name.

**Probe MT2** (ev:ev-mv4f1mox-01c9b0c9). Capture-compensation's RS-22 line was marked `# SKIP` in a copy of the cited log. The evidence-table test stays green (11/11), because execute.test.js's same-prefix test satisfies both entries.

**The check itself works:** MT1 is red.

findings.title: README one-command demo: the sample text yields no cup diameter, so confirm is refused until the user enters 90 mm, a step the README does not mention
findings.detail:
**Run verbatim, on loopback, with a scratch database** (ev:ev-mv4f3zu2-011fdea3, a red run kept as the evidence). Extract returns diameterMm null, and confirm answers 422 REQUIREMENTS_INCOMPLETE {fields: [diameterMm]}.

**With 90 entered**, as the form asks, the README's claim holds: A+B at 8400 cents, C incompatible and D too late (ev:ev-mv4f4i78-01a3b26b).

**Impact.** A judge following the README meets an unexplained question.
findings.recommendation: Owner: orchestrator. The README's owners are closed, so this needs a decision, as for FU-60. Resolved when the README's sample text names the diameter (for example '..., 250 ml, 90 mm cups, ...') or tells the reader to enter 90 mm when asked, and a run of the documented journey confirms as written.

findings.title: (security, technical concurs) The RS-29 secrets scan does not cover everything the repository ships
findings.recommendation:
Owner: orchestrator (g3's file; release checklist). Resolved by either of the following:
(1) The scan is extended to every tracked or untracked-unignored file, including .eccode/, and to every PNG ancillary chunk, with a path allow-list for test sources that hold canaries by design; P-PLANT's ten misses are then reported.
(2) RS-29's row and the verification report are narrowed to the scanned scope, and docs/submission/checklist.md gains a pre-publication check of .eccode/evidence for raw credential values.

findings.title: (security, merges TR-G-4) T20 deviation accepted on condition: the SQL scan lets name reuse, .exec(variable), whitespace before the paren and bound aliases through
(merges SEC-G-I2) clean-checkout.sh copies the working tree including untracked files, does not seed, and its keep option is dead; derive.js row 12 also accepts `draft`
findings.detail:
**Clean checkout.**
- `git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard` copies untracked, unignored working-tree files. Security's CC-PROBE copied an untracked my-notes.txt (ev:ev-mv4f23u2-0180cb1e). My run and the delivery-lead's were on a clean HEAD.
- RS_KEEP_CLEAN_CHECKOUT=1 never works, because the script's own RS_* unset loop clears it first.
- The script does not run `npm run seed`. My README run seeded a fresh copy successfully.

**derive.js.** Row 12 lists `draft` beside proposed and approved. `draft` is a real plan status: a harmless totalising extension the table does not name.
findings.recommendation: No change required for this gate. Owner: delivery-lead (verification report) and, optionally, a maintenance change: copy --cached only (or refuse a dirty tree), and exempt the keep variable from the unset loop. Resolved when the report states the working-tree behaviour and the row-12 extension.

findings.title: (security) The NFR3 launcher test spawns run-live-paypal.js, which `npm run test:live-paypal` does not use
findings.detail: The real `npm run test:live-paypal` and `npm run test:live-model` both refuse without their flags, with no network attempt and no report written (ev:ev-mv4ewm10-01f01459). Near-miss flags refuse too (ev:ev-mv4ex31x-0112ab69).
findings.recommendation: Owner: orchestrator (follow-up). Resolved when the test is retitled and a test runs the real test:live-paypal command line under the guard.

findings.title: (security) RS-34 labels are honest in the two combinations g3 did not render
findings.detail: The README demo start (fake, no test mode) and the Sandbox label set without test mode were both rendered in Chromium at 360 and 1280. Nothing reads as live money, and no request left 127.0.0.1 (ev:ev-mv4f119i-01b75fe7).
findings.recommendation: No change. Resolved by the verification report citing it.

findings.title: (security) Documents: no live, compliance or savings claim; one wording nit
findings.detail: project-description.md L30 lists 'signature-verified webhooks' among the PayPal features, while the verification has met only the fake HMAC and the stub. The next bullet disclaims it.
findings.recommendation: Owner: the user (release checklist, FU-61). Resolved when L30 qualifies the claim inline ('tested against local stubs only').
